node-1.label: Patient presented with 1-month history of daily epigastric pain and rectal bleeding

node-2.label: 49-year-old man with past medical history of acquired immune deficiency syndrome (last CD4 count of 10 cells/mm³)

node-3.label: Physical exam revealed condyloma acuminata in the perianal region

why.why: New expert analyses from both the Pathologist and Laboratory Physician explicitly conclude that the 6 cm ulcerated polypoid rectal mass with mixed spindle/epithelioid cells is atypical for infection and strongly favors AIDS-associated malignancy. No pathogen-specific evidence has emerged, and CT showing nonspecific colitis does not change this assessment, so confidence is reduced from 0.1 to 0.05.

The Pathologist and Laboratory Physician both state that the colonoscopy finding of a 6 cm ulcerated polypoid rectal mass and biopsy showing mixed spindle/epithelioid cells, in a severely immunosuppressed patient with CD4 10, strongly supports AIDS-associated GI malignancy over infection. The new CT evidence of nonspecific colitis does not exclude malignancy. Confidence is raised from 0.65 to 0.75; it is not higher because IHC confirmation is still pending.

Expert analyses continue to classify perianal condyloma as secondary to the dominant rectal mass, and the colonoscopy finding of a 6 cm polypoid mass reduces the likelihood that HPV-related anal disease is the primary cause of bleeding. Confidence is reduced from 0.15 to 0.1.

node-7.label: Colonoscopy reveals a 6 cm ulcerated polypoid rectal mass

node-8.label: Biopsy of the rectal mass shows mixed spindle and epithelioid cells

node-9.label: Rectal mass is Kaposi sarcoma (AIDS-associated GI malignancy)

why.why: Both the Pathologist and Laboratory Physician identify Kaposi sarcoma as the leading specific diagnosis given the 6 cm ulcerated polypoid rectal mass with mixed spindle/epithelioid cells in a patient with CD4 10. The Pathologist notes IHC (HHV-8, CD31) is still required for definitive diagnosis, and the Laboratory Physician notes HHV-8, CD31, CD34, and S100 are unavailable. Confidence is raised from 0.55 to 0.7, reflecting strong morphological and clinical support while awaiting IHC confirmation.
